A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ECHO research work, with readable main text, figures, tables, equations, Appendices A–C, and Algorithm 1. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original text and multimodal reasoning experiments, component ablations, sensitivity studies, and rollout analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, failure analyses, and sampling-budget experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same branching and pruning procedures, majority-vote rewards, confidence-adaptive clipping, hybrid advantages, and optimization objective.

E1.justification: The text and visual reasoning benchmarks and training datasets are unchanged. This includes the ReClor and ThinkLite-11K distribution-mismatch scenarios in Appendix B.1.

E2.justification: TTRL, ETMR, EVOL-RL, INTUITOR, and MM-UPT retain their respective comparison roles. The supervised GRPO comparisons in Tables 11–12 are also unchanged; no corresponding experiment adds or removes a comparator.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics and reported settings remain unchanged, including 64 voting rollouts, 32 responses for training updates, and the 3,072-token response limit. Section 4.2 adds a '(Think)' label to Qwen3-8B without documenting a change to the experimental procedure.

E4.justification: The component ablations, training-dynamics and diversity analyses, pruning-threshold and window-size sweeps, distribution-mismatch studies, and Pass@K analyses are retained unchanged in Table 3, Tables 7–10, and Figures 4–7.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the figures and Table 4's statement about averaging over 32 rollouts. No repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All matched numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains ECHO's Qwen3-8B average of 76.1 after AIME2024 training, and Table 2 retains the Qwen3-VL-8B/GeoQA average of 60.5. Appendix results are also identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same lemmas, proposition, proofs, clipping-gate derivation, and KL-gradient analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion preserve the same claims about mitigating rollout collapse and pseudo-label overfitting and improving text and visual reasoning without external supervision.

C2.justification: The mechanism interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged. Appendix B.1 retains the limitations concerning premature pruning, insufficient task-specific priors, unreliable pseudo-labels, and negative transfer.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly identifies Qwen3-8B as '(Think)', although Appendix A.2 retains the Qwen3-8B-Base wording. New acknowledgements identify the computational-support provider. Implementation instructions, hyperparameter tables, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Rein et al. (2024) GPQA reference, leaving 'GPQA-Diamond (?)' in Appendix A.1. The remaining cited works, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgements, adds Jianzhe Zhao as a corresponding author, replaces the preprint notice with conference publication information, and makes small wording and heading edits. The scientific narrative and section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: The first-page footer changes, and local text reflow changes spacing and column/page breaks around Sections 4.3–6 and the references, including splitting the conclusion across pages 8–9. Figures and tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, results, and proofs are unchanged. The added model qualifier and support acknowledgements offer limited documentation benefits, but deleting the GPQA reference leaves an unresolved citation in Appendix A.1 and weakens source attribution. The net decline is small and concerns documentation and editorial completeness.
